Example Sentence: 길동은 아버지를 아버지라고 부르지 못해 슬퍼했다.
Sentence Translation: Gildong was sad because he could not call his father 'father'.

Example Sentence: 좁은 방에 오래 있으니 마음이 갑갑해요.
Sentence Translation: Being in a small room for a long time makes me feel suffocated.
Etymology: Pure Korean adjective describing emotional or physical stuffiness

Example Sentence: 이 상황에서 화가 나지 않을 수 있겠습니까?
Sentence Translation: How can one not get angry in this situation?

Example Sentence: 아픈 유기견들을 보면 마음이 너무 아파요.
Sentence Translation: When I see sick abandoned dogs, my heart aches deeply.
Etymology: 마음 (heart/mind) + 이 (subject marker) + 아프다 (to be sick/painful)

Example Sentence: 시험에 떨어질까 봐 밤새 공부했어요.
Sentence Translation: I studied all night for fear that I might fail the exam.
Etymology: ~ㄹ까 (shall we/wondering if) + 봐 (from 보다, to see/experience)

Example Sentence: 비가 너무 많이 와서 약속을 취소하는 것은 어쩔 수 없었어요.
English: it cannot be helped / no choice
Sentence Translation: It couldn't be helped that we canceled the appointment because it rained too much.
Etymology: 어찌할 (what to do) + 수 (way/method) + 없다 (to not exist)

Example Sentence: 내가 너를 얼마나 아끼는지 네가 잘 알지 않느냐.
Sentence Translation: Don't you know well how much I cherish you?

Example Sentence: 우리는 서로 도우며 살아가야 합니다.
English: to live on / to get along in life
Sentence Translation: We must live on while helping each other.
Etymology: 살다 (to live) + 아/어 가다 (to continue doing into the future)

Example Sentence: 괜한 소리 하지 말고 공부나 열심히 해라.
Sentence Translation: Do not say useless things and just study hard.

Example Sentence: 머리로는 알고는 있지만 마음대로 잘 안 돼요.
Sentence Translation: I do indeed know it with my head, but it doesn't work out the way I want.

Example Sentence: 노력한 만큼 결과가 안 나와서 너무 속상해요.
Sentence Translation: I am so upset because the results didn't turn out as much as I worked.

Example Sentence: 어두운 골목길을 걸을 때 안 좋은 느낌이 들었어요.
English: to get a bad feeling / ominous hunch
Sentence Translation: I got a bad feeling when walking down the dark alleyway.
Etymology: 안 좋은 (not good) + 느낌 (feeling) + 이 (subject marker) + 들다 (to enter)

Example Sentence: 소방관들이 화재 현장에 도착해서 재빨리 불을 껐어요.
Sentence Translation: The firefighters arrived at the fire scene and quickly put out the fire.

Example Sentence: 욕심 많은 형이 동생의 장난감을 빼앗았어요.
English: to snatch / take away by force
Sentence Translation: The greedy older brother snatched his younger brother's toy away.

Example Sentence: 그때 제가 말했던 것은 다 거짓말이었던 거예요.
English: It was because... / The fact is...
Sentence Translation: The fact is, everything I said at that time was a lie.

Example Sentence: 열심히 연습해야 시험에 합격할 수 있어요.
English: only if / must... in order to
Sentence Translation: Only if you practice hard can you pass the exam.
Etymology: Connective particle establishing an essential condition

Example Sentence: 어디선가 달콤한 냄새가 풍겨왔어요.
Sentence Translation: A sweet smell drifted in from somewhere.

Example Sentence: 컴퓨터에서 이상한 소리가 나기 시작했어요.
English: to make a sound / a sound occurs
Sentence Translation: A strange sound started coming out from the computer.

Example Sentence: 매일 운동을 해 보니 몸이 아주 가벼워졌어요.
Sentence Translation: Upon exercising every day, I found that my body became very light.
Etymology: ~고 보니 / ~어 보니 (try doing and discovering a result)

Example Sentence: 저는 한국어 말하기 시험에 자신 있어요.
Sentence Translation: I am confident in the Korean speaking test.

Example Sentence: 그는 자신의 잘못을 당당하게 인정했어요.
Sentence Translation: He confidently acknowledged his mistake.

Example Sentence: 오늘 아주 피곤해 보이는데 무슨 일 있어요?
English: to look like / appear to be
Sentence Translation: You look very tired today; is something the matter?

Example Sentence: 역도는 무거운 바벨을 번쩍 들어 올렸어요.
English: to lift up with ease in one motion
Sentence Translation: The weightlifter lifted the heavy barbell up with ease.
Etymology: 번쩍 (mimetic word for sudden/effortless lift) + 들어 올리다 (to lift up)

Example Sentence: 아이가 엄마에게 장난감을 사 달라고 했어요.
English: to ask someone to do a favor
Sentence Translation: The child asked their mother to buy a toy for them.
Etymology: ~어 주다 (to do for someone) + 달라고 (requesting for self) + 하다 (to say/ask)

Example Sentence: 경찰이 나쁜 행동을 한 도둑을 혼내주었어요.
English: to punish / teach a lesson / scold
Sentence Translation: The police punished the thief who did bad deeds.
Etymology: 혼 (spirit/mind) + 내다 (to draw out) + 주다 (to give the action)

Example Sentence: 친구에게 빌린 책을 오늘 돌려주었어.
Sentence Translation: I returned the book I borrowed from my friend today.

Example Sentence: 우리 같이 열심히 공부해 봅시다.
Sentence Translation: Let's try studying hard together.

Example Sentence: 대한민국 만세! 라고 사람들이 외쳤다.
Sentence Translation: People shouted, 'Long live the Republic of Korea!'
Etymology: 萬歲 (Sino-Korean: Ten thousand years of longevity/prosperity)

Example Sentence: 이번에는 반드시 약속을 지키겠습니다.
English: without fail / certainly / by all means
Sentence Translation: This time, I will keep my promise without fail.
Etymology: Pure Korean adverb indicating absolute certainty

Example Sentence: 외출하려고 하자 갑자기 비가 내리기 시작했어요.
English: just as someone was about to / when trying to
Sentence Translation: Just as I was about to go out, it suddenly started to rain.

Example Sentence: 도사님이 신기한 도술을 부려 비를 내리게 했다.
Sentence Translation: The Taoist master performed marvelous magic to make it rain.
Etymology: 도술 (道術: supernatural art) + 을 + 부리다 (to practice/wield/manage)

Example Sentence: 그 쌍둥이는 얼굴이 똑같이 생겼어요.
Sentence Translation: Those twins look exactly identical in the face.
Etymology: 똑같이 (exactly the same) + 생기다 (to look like/appear)

Example Sentence: 봄이 오자 길가에 이곳저곳 꽃이 피었습니다.
Sentence Translation: As spring arrived, flowers bloomed here and there along the roadside.

Example Sentence: 선생님이 교실에 들어오시자 학생들이 조용해졌어요.
Sentence Translation: As soon as the teacher entered the classroom, the students became quiet.

Example Sentence: 그는 진로 문제 때문에 깊은 고민에 빠졌어요.
English: to fall into deep worry / dilemma
Sentence Translation: He fell into deep worry due to his career path options.
Etymology: 고민 (苦悶: agony/worry) + 에 (into) + 빠지다 (to fall/sink)

Example Sentence: 약을 먹었는데 오히려 병이 더 심해진 것 같아요.
Sentence Translation: I took medicine, but on the contrary, the illness seems to have become worse.
Etymology: Pure Korean adverb indicating an unexpected contrast

Example Sentence: 그 영웅은 나라를 위해 목숨을 바쳤습니다.
English: for the country / for the sake of the nation
Sentence Translation: The hero sacrificed his life for the country.
Etymology: 나라 (country) + 를 + 위해 (for the sake of)

Example Sentence: 날씨가 추우니 따뜻한 외투를 입어야겠다.
English: I should / I must / think I will have to
Sentence Translation: Since the weather is cold, I think I should wear a warm coat.

Example Sentence: 그녀는 환하게 웃으며 나에게 인사를 건넸다.
Sentence Translation: She handed me a greeting while smiling brightly.
Etymology: Connective particle for concurrent states or actions

Example Sentence: 그들은 새로운 삶을 찾아 바다를 건너 이주했습니다.
Sentence Translation: They crossed the sea and migrated in search of a new life.
